A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LoRA-Ensemble study. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching material relocated between versions.

before.justification: v2 reports original classification, calibration, OOD detection, computational-cost, and ablation results across its main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds SVHN evaluation, diversity diagnostics, a high-rank control, and temperature-scaling results.

M1.justification: Section 2 retains the frozen shared backbone, member-specific low-rank attention updates and classification heads, and prediction averaging. Temperature scaling is investigated separately rather than incorporated into the proposed method.

E1.justification: v3 adds SVHN as an OOD test dataset alongside the existing CIFAR-100/CIFAR-10 setting in Table 5. Classification coverage on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, HAM10000, and ESC-50 is retained.

E2.justification: Appendix A.4 adds a rank-128 single-LoRA control matched to the ensemble's LoRA-matrix parameter budget; Appendix E adds temperature-scaled comparisons. Existing baseline families remain. Split-Ensemble already appeared in v2's OOD comparison.

E3.justification: v3 adds substantive evaluation designs: the high-rank capacity control, fixed-weight temperature sweeps, and diversity assessment using prediction disagreement, Jensen-Shannon divergence, spectral comparisons, and training trajectories. These extend the evaluation protocol; retained benchmark settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: New Section 4 and Appendix D examine diversity in predictions, weights, singular vectors, and training trajectories. Appendices A.4 and E test parameter capacity and temperature sensitivity. Earlier rank, model-size, initialization, noise, and dropout analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five independent runs with different random initializations and one-sigma error bars. No revised run counts, seed practices, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures are reported.

E6.justification: Original numerical benchmark results are retained. New results include SVHN LoRA-Ensemble AUROC/AUPRC of 89.9/80.9 (Table 5), rank-128 single-LoRA accuracy of 77.0% (Table 7), temperature-dependent calibration (Table 9), and greater measured ensemble diversity (Figures 2, 3, and 9-12).

T1.justification: v3 adds mathematical definitions for the new disagreement diagnostic and temperature-scaling transformation, plus an SVD formulation for the spectral analysis. Existing LoRA equations and evaluation-metric definitions remain unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The introduction adds an explicit contribution concerning explanation of performance through function-space and weight-space diversity. The abstract and conclusion retain the original efficiency, applicability, and predictive-performance claims.

C2.justification: v3 expands the parameter-constraint explanation with broader weight-space exploration and near-orthogonal 'intruder dimensions,' and argues that parameter count alone cannot explain the gains. It also removes v2's explicit limitation that convergence to distinct modes lacks theoretical proof.

D1.justification: v3 documents new analysis details, including top-16 singular-vector comparisons, averaging across layers and members, checkpoints every five epochs from 5 to 65, control-model parameter counts, and temperature grids. Existing training details and the promised code/weight release remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations supporting SVHN, t-SNE, diversity analysis, Packed-Ensembles, and Shuttleworth et al.'s LoRA spectral interpretation. These extend the discussion while retaining the main research positioning. The two Fort 2019 entries represent an already cited work.

P1.justification: Editing is concentrated in the introduction, OOD discussion, and mechanism/limitations passages. Rank sensitivity is consolidated in Appendix C, related-work subheadings are reformatted, and new analysis sections are inserted. Most existing prose and narrative order remain.

P2.justification: v3 adds six diversity-related figures, two tables, and SVHN columns in Table 5. Original CIFAR-100 plots move to Appendix A.2, and separate rank-sensitivity figures are merged into Figure 8. All original plots are retained, substantially reorganizing their presentation.

improvement.justification: The diversity diagnostics and LoRA-budget control strengthen v2's largely heuristic explanation, while SVHN and temperature sweeps broaden validation. The improvement is limited by the observational nature of the mechanism evidence and removal of v2's explicit no-proof caveat. Overall, v3 provides stronger empirical support, with less cautious interpretation of what that support establishes.
